scope: Declaration of the shared evaluation frame used by every record in this file.
note: Gates G1 (categorical non-confusion) and G2 (single authority) are non-tradeable: any candidate failing a gate is disqualified regardless of other scores. Objectives O1-O12 and materiality thresholds M1-M7 are defined once in PHASE-2-CREATOR-AXIOMS.md section 4 and are not restated per record; each record names only the objectives that materially discriminate among its candidates. Per C8, implementation effort, delivery time, code volume, monetary cost and familiarity never appear in any objective vector. Per C10, no record claims optimality.
dominance_challenge_protocol: After each provisional selection, construct a candidate claimed to be no worse on every declared material objective and materially better on at least one. If the claim survives scrutiny, replace the provisional selection and repeat. Every iteration is recorded with its outcome, including failures.
totals_note: Totals are NOT restated here. They are derived mechanically from this file by the sealing script and recorded only in PHASE-2-MANIFEST.json and PHASE-2-SEAL.json. The architecture's own rule is applied to the architecture's own documents: the counts are derived, and if they cannot be derived they are labelled hand-asserted.

decision_class: institutional authority and separation of powers
scope: How authority to bring about institutional facts is held, delegated, checked and bounded inside the Watchtower.
operating_model: OA-5: operators are trusted for availability, not for integrity. Faults F12 (operator tampering), F14 (charter amendment error).

candidates.name: Flat monolith with implicit authority
candidates.description: One process, one write path; separation of concerns by module boundary only. Authority is whatever the code permits.

candidates.name: Deliberative agent council with voting
candidates.description: N peer agents propose and vote; majority admits. Authority is emergent from aggregation.

candidates.name: Chartered offices holding exclusive typed powers, acts void without warrant
candidates.description: A constitutional charter enumerates offices; each fact class has exactly one empowered office; every act presents a warrant checked at admission; an unempowered act is void, not merely rejected. Counts-as relations classify brute acts as institutional acts in context.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-010 institutionalised power; RL-002 constitutive vs regulative norms

candidates.name: Object-capability model without a constitution
candidates.description: Authority is possession of unforgeable capability references; no central charter; delegation by reference passing.

evidence_required: A formal characterisation showing that (i) power can be typed and exclusive, (ii) an act by an unempowered agent can be made to have no institutional effect, and (iii) the classification of a brute act as institutional is itself a checkable relation.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D01-d object-capability without charter
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on G1/G2, better on O9 because capability possession is mechanically checkable without a charter interpreter.
dominance_challenges.reason: Capabilities check possession, not entitlement. They cannot express exclusivity (that exactly one office may issue a fact class) because a capability can be copied and delegated without limit, and they cannot express entrenchment (A10). Loss on G2 and O4 is material under M6. The mechanism is nevertheless adopted inside D01-c as the representation of a warrant.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D01-c plus mandatory dual-office countersignature on every act
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse anywhere, better on O9 by removing single-office capture.
dominance_challenges.reason: Countersignature on every act is not no-worse: it destroys the exclusivity property that makes single-authority checkable (two offices signing a fact class means two offices hold the power), a material loss on G2 under M6. Adopted narrowly instead, for charter amendment only, where exclusivity is not claimed.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D01-c plus entrenched clauses and an inspection power that can suspend but never create
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse anywhere, better on O4 because a bounded amendment power removes the hidden universal authority latent in an unbounded one.
dominance_challenges.reason: Adopted as axiom A10 and invariant I-34. Without entrenchment the amendment power can remove any invariant, so the amendment office silently holds every power. The Inspectorate is given a purely negative power so that it cannot become a second Tribunal.

final_selection: D01-c + entrenchment (A10) + negative-only inspection power
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Entrenchment binds internal acts only. An operator with filesystem write access defeats it; the design converts that from prevention to detection (external anchoring, witness co-signature) and states the limit rather than concealing it.

decision_class: institutional authority and separation of powers (enforcement mechanism)
scope: By what mechanism is 'an act without power has no institutional effect' actually enforced, as opposed to intended.

candidates.name: Convention plus code review
candidates.description: Authority rules documented; adherence by discipline.

candidates.name: Runtime assertions at service entry points
candidates.description: Each entry point checks a permission table before proceeding.

candidates.name: Custom method combination with warrant objects, plus package hygiene
candidates.description: Institutional acts are generic functions using a user-defined method combination in which a :warrant qualifier group must unanimously succeed before any primary method is executed; office internals are unexported and packages are locked so that the only cross-office call path is the protocol; the warrant is a first-class object recorded with the act.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-042 define-method-combination long form; RL-038 SBCL package facilities

candidates.name: Static declarations and type checks only
candidates.description: declaim/deftype constraints checked at compile time.

candidates.name: Admission-side warrant reconstruction, evaluated in the verification kernel
candidates.description: Enforcement sits at the single append point, not at call sites. The gate is a pure, total, ACL2-admitted function admit-p(charter, entry) evaluated by V_w, which imports no office package. It does not trust the caller's warrant object; it independently reconstructs from the Charter power table whether office(entry) holds issue(kind, fact-class), and then requires the presented warrant to be a Charter-derived capability bound to the entry's content digest.
candidates.added_by: second audit round, finding HF-022 (closes DF-002)

evidence_required: A language mechanism that can prevent the primary behaviour from running at all when the warrant check fails, rather than detecting the violation afterwards.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D02-c method combination
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse than D02-b anywhere, better on O9 because the check is part of effective-method computation rather than the first line of a body, so it cannot be forgotten in a new method and cannot be bypassed by a direct call to the primary.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. DEFINE-METHOD-COMBINATION's long form computes the effective method from the applicable methods and their qualifiers, so 'no primary runs unless all :warrant methods succeed' is a property of the generic function, not of any method body (RL-042). Material under M6: the authority boundary becomes enforced rather than conventional.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D02-c plus a MOP-level generic-function class refusing method addition without a warrant method
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse: it forbids legitimate :around methods used for recording and for institutional context binding, reducing expressible institutional behaviour. Superseded by a weaker rule adopted instead: an ADD-METHOD audit reports any institutional generic function whose applicable-method set lacks a warrant method, checked at image build.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D02-c restricted to ANSI-only mechanisms (drop SBCL-specific facilities)
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on gates, better on portability.
dominance_challenges.reason: Portability is not in the objective vector (C8 excludes familiarity and convenience; portability enters only where it serves O9 verifiability). NOTE (third audit round, HF-028): the original reason given here rested on claim WC-6, which is withdrawn. The challenge still fails, for a different reason: dropping SBCL-specific facilities removes the package/system closure computation on which the I-42 kernel-disjointness audit depends (PO-042), and I-42 is what makes the I-41 self-verification remedy checkable. Material under M3.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D02-e admission-side warrant reconstruction evaluated in the verification kernel
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse anywhere, materially better on G1, G2 and O9, because admission becomes a pure function of (Charter, entry) that quantifies over ENTRIES rather than over CALL PATHS, and is therefore provable and insensitive to how the producing code was written.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. This closes DF-002 rather than bounding it. The first selection made the architecture's central authority guarantee depend on a mechanism that a single ordinary in-office function call defeats, and on package locks an office can lift on its own package; the second audit round (finding HF-022) judged that acceptance to have been an error. The gate no longer CHECKS a caller-supplied warrant: it RECONSTRUCTS from the Charter whether this office holds this power over this fact class, then requires the presented warrant to be a Charter-derived capability bound to the entry's content digest. Discharged as PO-046: for all e, committed(e) implies charter-permits(office(e), kind(e), fact-class(e)). D02-c is retained as defence in depth because failing fast at the call site with a good diagnostic is worth having; it is no longer what makes the invariant true.

final_selection: D02-e (authoritative, at the append point, evaluated in V_w) with D02-c retained as defence in depth
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Admission is only as good as the Charter it reconstructs from, and the reconstruction runs in V_w, so a defect in the shared specification or the frozen decoders defeats it (DF-043). What is no longer true is that a bypassing call path defeats it.
revision_note: Revised in the second audit round. The first version's final_selection was D02-c with DF-002 accepted as BOUNDED.

scope: What identifies a normative unit, a textual version, a published rendering and a byte sequence, and which of these may confer any of the others.

candidates.name: URL as identity
candidates.description: The retrieval URL identifies the document.

candidates.name: Content digest as identity
candidates.description: The hash of the retrieved bytes is the identity.

candidates.name: Four-level identity: Registry-assigned norm identity over ELI/AKN expression and WEMI manifestation over digest
candidates.description: Norm identity is institutional and assigned only by the Registry; expression identity aligns to ELI and the Akoma Ntoso naming convention; manifestation follows IFLA LRM; digest identifies bytes. No function maps digest to norm identity.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-003 ELI, RL-054 AKN naming convention, RL-029 IFLA LRM

candidates.name: Opaque local UUID with a mapping table
candidates.description: Internal UUIDs, externally mapped.

evidence_required: A standard identity scheme that distinguishes the abstract work from its textual versions and from physical renderings, plus evidence that external identifier authorities exist and are defeasible.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D03-c but adopting Greek ELI identifiers as authoritative norm identity when available
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O10 interoperability because the Watchtower would use the state's own identifiers.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Greek ELI implementation status, URI policy and stability were not verifiable in this phase (RL-055), and an externally minted identifier adopted as authoritative would make an external system the authority over a Watchtower fact class, violating G2. Adopted in weakened form: external ELI identifiers are recorded as defeasible external assertions bound to Registry norm identity (I-10), which preserves interoperability without transferring authority.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D03-b digest identity, on the ground that it is the only identity that cannot be wrong
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O1 because a hash is verifiable.
dominance_challenges.reason: A hash is verifiable and legally useless: under L5 a lawful correction produces a different digest for the same norm, and two identical byte sequences may manifest different norms in different contexts. Digest identity makes I-13 unsatisfiable. Material under M1.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D03-c with norm identity assigned by the Tribunal rather than the Registry
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on G1 by concentrating adjudication.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse: it merges the identity power and the authority power in one office, which is exactly the separation I-09 exists to prevent. Material under M6.

final_selection: D03-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Norm identity for Greek instruments is a Watchtower assertion where no stable national identifier exists. Its correctness is defeasible and is exactly the kind of claim I-10 requires to carry a reopening predicate.

scope: What makes a source or an instrument authoritative, and where that determination is computed.

candidates.name: Per-source trust score
candidates.description: Each source carries a numeric trust weight; authority is a weighted function.

candidates.name: Boolean authoritative flag per source
candidates.description: Sources are marked authoritative or not.

candidates.name: Authority as a derived relation over (organ, instrument type, legal order, time) x evidentiary status x confirmed identity
candidates.description: Authority is never an attribute of a document or a channel; it is a relation computed by the kernel from the organ that issued the instrument, the instrument type, the legal order and the time, combined with evidentiary status and Registry-confirmed identity.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-021 Art. 26 separation of powers; RL-013 temporal norm change; RL-002 LegalRuleML norm classification

candidates.name: Per-document manual designation
candidates.description: A human marks each document's authority.

evidence_required: Legal evidence that authority varies with the issuing organ and the instrument type independently of the retrieval channel.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D04-a numeric trust score
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 because a number is cheap to compute and compose.
dominance_challenges.reason: A single number cannot represent that a ministerial decision published in Gazette series B is authoritative for its own subject matter and simultaneously incapable of altering a statute. Composition of trust scores silently produces authority laundering, violating A4 and I-02. Material under M1. Also O12 is Tier 4 and cannot offset a Tier 1 loss.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D04-c with a precomputed authority cache keyed by instrument
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted as an implementation of the derived state, not as a change of authority: the cache is a derived store subject to the deletability test (A8, I-31). Recorded because it demonstrates that a performance measure is admissible precisely when it cannot become an authority.

final_selection: D04-c with derived authority cache subject to I-31
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The organ-to-authority mapping for the Greek order must be curated and is itself defeasible; errors are legal-classification errors, detectable only by adjudication, not by the kernel.

scope: How legal time is represented so that point-in-time reconstruction, retroactivity, per-provision commencement, abrogation, annulment and correction are all expressible.

candidates.name: Bitemporal (valid time + transaction time)
candidates.description: Two axes as in the temporal database tradition.

candidates.name: SQL:2011 system-versioned plus application-time period tables
candidates.description: Standardised bitemporality in the DBMS.

candidates.name: Document-version snapshots
candidates.description: One immutable document per amendment event; time handled by choosing a snapshot.

candidates.name: Nine-axis model at provision granularity, every axis an adjudicated defeasible proposition, with abrogation/annulment/correction trichotomy
candidates.description: t_enact, t_promulgate, t_publish, t_force, t_apply_from, t_apply_to, t_end, plus system axes t_observe, t_record, t_believe; commencement is per provision; defaults such as the ten-day rule are named defeasible inference rules, not stored values.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-021 Art. 42; RL-023 EisNAK Art. 103; RL-013 abrogation vs annulment; RL-026 correction procedure

evidence_required: Legal evidence that (i) publication and entry into force are distinct, (ii) commencement varies per provision, (iii) cessation kinds differ in temporal effect, (iv) published text can lawfully change after the fact.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D05-d nine-axis adjudicated model
dominance_challenges.claim: Materially better on O2 and O3; worse only on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Bitemporality cannot express per-provision commencement, retroactive applicability distinct from validity, or the ex tunc / ex nunc distinction between annulment and abrogation (RL-013). Under M1 this changes the admissibility of every point-in-time proposition about a partially-commenced statute, which is the common case in Greek legislation. The O12 loss is Tier 4 and is not material under M7 at the declared corpus scale (OA-4).

dominance_challenges.challenger: D05-d with dates stored as scalars and only disputed dates promoted to propositions
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse in the normal case, better on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Whether a date is disputed is not knowable in advance; promotion on dispute requires rewriting history for facts already published, which A2 forbids. The uniform representation is what makes correction expressible as an append. Material under M5.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D05-d plus an interval algebra with explicit open/closed and unknown endpoints
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O2 and O10 because 'in force from an unknown date after publication' is representable.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted. Unknown endpoints are common (commencement 'on publication of a further ministerial decision'). Without them the system must either guess or refuse; with them it can answer precisely about what it does not know, which is required by R-10.

final_selection: D05-d with explicit interval endpoints including UNKNOWN
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Nine axes are argued sufficient for the Greek order as characterised by L1, L2, L5, L6; sufficiency is not proved. A tenth axis (e.g. distinct treatment of suspension of effect, anastoli) may prove necessary; the model is extensible because axes are propositions, not columns.

scope: How the chain from observation to derived text is represented so that it is verifiable, exportable and impossible to launder.

candidates.name: W3C PROV graph as the internal model
candidates.description: Entities, activities, agents in RDF.

candidates.name: in-toto/DSSE attestations as the internal model
candidates.description: Signed predicates about subjects.

candidates.name: Native lineage records over content-addressed artifacts with preserved source containers, exported to PROV and in-toto
candidates.description: Internal model is a typed CLOS lineage graph carrying evidentiary status and transformation identity; source-signed containers are retained unmodified; export mappings to PROV-O and in-toto exist but are not the authority.

candidates.name: Implicit lineage from the log
candidates.description: No explicit lineage records; reconstruct from event order.

evidence_required: A representation that can express degradation of evidentiary strength under transformation. PROV's derivation relation is untyped with respect to fidelity.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D06-c native typed lineage
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on interoperability because export is lossless in the needed direction, materially better on O1 because degradation can be typed and proved.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. PROV can state that y was derived from x but cannot state that the derivation weakened evidentiary strength (RL-059), so the monotone-degradation theorem PO-004 is not expressible in PROV. Material under M3: the difference is between a provable invariant and a documented convention.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D06-c without container retention, storing only container digests and signatures
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on storage.
dominance_challenges.reason: Storage is excluded by C8. Under L5 the source may lawfully replace the container; without the retained bytes I-13 fails and past answers become unexplainable. Material under M5.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D06-c plus third-party custody attestations
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O1 against operator tampering.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted. Derived from the rejected synthesis CCF (Candidates section 8): an independent attestation that a digest was held at a time adds evidence the Watchtower cannot manufacture about itself. Adopted as an additional control, never as a replacement for custody.

final_selection: D06-c with retained containers plus third-party custody attestations
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Export fidelity to PROV is claimed only for the subset PROV can express; the degradation lattice is exported as custom qualified properties and a consumer ignoring them will read a weaker but not false graph.

scope: The algebraic structure of evidentiary strength.

candidates.name: Numeric confidence score
candidates.description: Strength in [0,1].

candidates.name: Boolean authentic / not authentic
candidates.description: Two values.

candidates.name: Finite partial order (lattice) with an absorbing bottom and an incomparable doctrinal branch
candidates.description: UNVERIFIED, SECONDARY, AUTHENTIC-UNSIGNED, AUTHENTIC-SIGNED, AUTHENTIC-SIGNED-ANCHORED in a chain; DOCTRINAL incomparable; DISPUTED as meet; REPUDIATED absorbing.

candidates.name: Probabilistic (Bayesian) evidence model
candidates.description: Strength as posterior probability of authenticity.

evidence_required: Legal grounding for at least three distinguishable strengths, and grounding for treating doctrine as a different kind rather than a weaker degree.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D07-a numeric score
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O10 because a number is easy to communicate.
dominance_challenges.reason: A number invites arithmetic, and arithmetic on evidentiary strength is exactly laundering: a pair of SECONDARY sources does not average into an AUTHENTIC one. The meet operation in a lattice has no such affordance. Material under M1. Communicability is not in the objective vector.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D07-d probabilistic
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O3 because uncertainty composes principledly.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A probability requires a reference class; there is none for 'this gazette signature is genuine'. Producing a number without a reference class would be a claim exceeding its evidence, which the acceptance contract forbids. Retained in one narrow place instead: calibration of source cadence models (D15), where a reference class does exist.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D07-c with DOCTRINAL placed below SECONDARY rather than incomparable
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9 by making the order total and therefore trivially checkable.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Placing doctrine in the authentic chain permits an argument to substitute a large amount of doctrine for a small amount of authority, which I-20 forbids. Incomparability is what makes PO-020 provable. Material under M3.

final_selection: D07-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence; the candidate domain is argued near-exhaustive because any strength representation is either ordered totally, ordered partially, numeric, or boolean, and all four families were evaluated.
residual_uncertainty: Whether five ranks plus two special elements suffice. A sixth rank (e.g. 'authenticated by re-observation from an independent channel') is plausible and would extend the chain without altering the theorems, since PO-004 is proved over the order, not over its cardinality.

scope: How beliefs are held, defeated, and explained.

candidates.name: Justification-based TMS (JTMS)
candidates.description: Single consistent context with dependency-directed backtracking.

candidates.name: Assumption-based TMS (ATMS)
candidates.description: Environments and labels, all consistent contexts simultaneously, minimal no-goods.

candidates.name: ASPIC+ structured argumentation alone
candidates.description: Strict and defeasible rules, three attack forms, preferences, abstract semantics.

candidates.name: ATMS substrate with ASPIC+ adjudication and an explicit LABEL-INCOMPLETE status
candidates.description: ATMS environments are the premise sets of ASPIC+ arguments; label propagation gives automatic defeat; argumentation gives the reason a jurist needs; a declared bound turns exponential blowup into a named status rather than silent truncation.

candidates.name: Probabilistic/Bayesian belief network
candidates.description: Beliefs as random variables with conditional dependencies.

candidates.name: No belief store; recompute on demand
candidates.description: Stateless derivation for each query.

candidates.name: Defeasible Logic proper (rule-based sceptical non-monotonic logic with a superiority relation)
candidates.description: Strict rules, defeasible rules, defeaters and an explicit superiority relation over rules; sceptical conclusions computed by a linear-time algorithm over the rule set; the formalism underlying LegalRuleML's defeasibility and the temporalised norm-change work.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-002 LegalRuleML defeasibility and rule superiority; RL-013 temporalised defeasible logic
candidates.added_by: hostile-audit finding HF-017 — this contender was materially distinct from D08-c and was omitted from the first pass

evidence_required: Evidence that (i) defeat can propagate without global recomputation, (ii) conflicting legal readings can coexist without inconsistency, (iii) rationality postulates are attainable, (iv) the computational cost is bounded or the incompleteness is nameable.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D08-d ATMS + ASPIC+ + declared incompleteness
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on any objective, materially better on O3 and O10 because an ATMS label says under which assumptions a belief holds but never says which of two conflicting legal readings prevails or why.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. The two mechanisms answer different questions and neither subsumes the other. ASPIC+ supplies defeat by preference and the rationality postulates (RL-008); the ATMS supplies incremental defeat propagation and no-goods (RL-009). Material under M5: without argument structure the system cannot explain a reversal.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D08-f recompute on demand
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on correctness, better on O5 by eliminating stored belief state entirely.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Recomputation cannot detect that a newly acquired defeater has invalidated a previously published answer, because nothing records that the answer was ever held. That is the reflective-memory requirement C5 and invariant I-26. Material under M5. Note that CDAI's belief store is derived (A8-compliant), so it does not carry D08-f's claimed benefit as a cost.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D08-d restricted to grounded semantics only
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O5 and O12 because grounded is unique and polynomial.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted as the admitted default. Grounded semantics is computable by a total function with a decreasing measure and is therefore ACL2-admissible, which preserves A3. Preferred-semantics questions are answered only under an explicit bounded search with a SEMANTICS-INCOMPLETE status. This is the honest resolution of the A3 falsifier.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D08-e probabilistic belief network
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O3 by quantifying uncertainty.
dominance_challenges.reason: Requires conditional probability tables for legal-interpretive dependencies for which no reference class exists; producing them would be a claim exceeding its evidence. Also destroys explanation: a posterior is not a reason. Material loss on O10 under M5.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D08-g Defeasible Logic proper, substituted for the ASPIC+ adjudication layer
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on O3 (it is a defeasibility formalism with an explicit superiority relation, which is precisely what I-19 needs), materially better on O5, O9 and O12 because sceptical Defeasible Logic has a linear-time extension algorithm, is trivially total and therefore ACL2-admissible without a bound, and would eliminate the SEMANTICS-INCOMPLETE and LABEL-INCOMPLETE statuses entirely.
dominance_challenges.reason: The efficiency and totality claims are correct and material, and this was the strongest challenge mounted against D08. It nevertheless fails on O10 under M5 and on O3 under M1. (i) Defeasible Logic yields a conclusion plus a proof tag, not an argument with an attack structure; the three ASPIC+ attack forms — undermining a premise, undercutting an inference, rebutting a conclusion — collapse into rule-level superiority, so the institution can report that a reading lost but not on which of the three grounds it lost. Under R-10 an answer must carry the defeaters considered and their disposition; that is not recoverable from a proof tag. (ii) Sceptical Defeasible Logic gives no representation of maximal-consistent readings, so the ATMS environments that CDAI uses to enumerate positions for a docket (I-25) and to reason about which assumptions are load-bearing for blind-spot analysis have no counterpart. Adopted partially instead: the superiority relation is the concrete form of the declared preference ordering in I-19, and the rule-classification discipline (strict vs defeasible vs defeater) is taken from this formalism rather than invented, which is why the strict/defeasible classification is listed among the Amendment-Council-amendable Charter provisions.

final_selection: D08-d with grounded semantics admitted by default, bounded preferred search flagged SEMANTICS-INCOMPLETE, LABEL-INCOMPLETE on bound exhaustion, and the rule-superiority discipline of Defeasible Logic adopted as the concrete form of the I-19 preference ordering
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The bound B_label is a policy parameter with no principled value; it is set empirically and its exhaustion frequency is itself a self-model proposition subject to A6.

decision_class: epistemic truth maintenance and defeaters (conflict meta-norms)
scope: How conflicts between legal conclusions are resolved.

candidates.name: Hard-coded priority order in code
candidates.description: Fixed resolution rules.

candidates.name: Learned preference from a corpus of decisions
candidates.description: Statistical ranking of which reading usually wins.

candidates.name: Declarative preference relation over rules, with lex superior, lex specialis and lex posterior encoded as themselves-defeasible meta-rules
candidates.description: The ordering is data, inspectable and attackable in a docket; unresolved conflict yields UNDECIDED rather than an arbitrary winner.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-008 preferences; RL-002 rule superiority; RL-013 norm change

evidence_required: Evidence that legal meta-norms are contested rather than absolute, so that hard-coding them would embed a legal position in the machinery.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D09-b learned preference
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 and on coverage of unanticipated conflicts.
dominance_challenges.reason: Violates A9: a learned ranking would decide legal outcomes, which is propositional authority for a statistical component. Also unexplainable, a material loss on O10 under M5.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D09-c plus automatic resolution by recency when the declared ordering is silent
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 by eliminating UNDECIDED outcomes.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Silent recency resolution is precisely the arbitrary tie-break I-19 forbids and would make the system assert a legal position it has no warrant for. UNDECIDED is the correct output and is publishable as a structured refusal (I-36).

final_selection: D09-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates; the candidate domain is argued exhaustive because a resolution policy is either fixed in code, learned from data, or declared as inspectable data, and all three were evaluated.
residual_uncertainty: That lex superior > lex specialis > lex posterior is the correct default ordering for the Greek legal order is a normative-legal claim, not a formal one. The architecture makes it inspectable and attackable, which is the strongest available treatment, not a proof.

decision_class: durable state and recovery (system of record)
scope: What is the single authority for institutional truth, and what is derived.

candidates.name: Relational DBMS as the authority
candidates.description: PostgreSQL or equivalent holds normalised legal state.

candidates.name: Prevalence: in-memory CLOS objects, transaction log, periodic snapshot
candidates.description: The live image is the truth; log and snapshot exist to restore it.

candidates.name: Append-only hash-chained entry log plus content-addressed artifact store, with all state derived by a pure versioned kernel
candidates.description: Two authorities only, disjoint by kind; every other store is derived and must pass the deletability test.
candidates.reconstructed_from: synthesis grounded in RL-011, RL-031, RL-017

candidates.name: RDF quadstore as the authority
candidates.description: Triples with named graphs for provenance.

candidates.name: Embedded key-value store as the authority
candidates.description: LMDB-style ordered KV as system of record.

evidence_required: Evidence that a log-plus-derived-state arrangement recovers correctly, and that MOP-mediated persistence in Common Lisp is a proven technique rather than an aspiration.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D10-c log plus content-addressed artifacts plus derived state
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on liveness at the declared corpus scale, materially better on O5, O8 and G2.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Under prevalence the live image is the authority (RL-045), which fails A12 and makes the deletability test A8 inapplicable, so G2 becomes unverifiable. Prevalence also has no answer to kernel-version evolution: replaying a log under a changed transaction function silently rewrites history. Material under M3 and M5. The mechanisms of prevalence (MOP-enforced transactional slot access, log plus snapshot, restart replay) are retained; only the authority relation is inverted.

dominance_challenges.challenger: Chartered Custodial Federation: charter and offices as in CDAI but holding no artifacts, relying on third-party custody attestations
dominance_challenges.claim: Strictly better on G2 because a system holding no corpus cannot hold a competing truth.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse elsewhere. Three material losses: I-13 becomes unsatisfiable under lawful source correction (M1); digest anti-entropy against a retained copy becomes impossible, removing a class of detectable blind spot (M2); and replay requires the input bytes, so state = K(record) fails outright, defeating A3 (M4/M5). Recorded in full in PHASE-2-CANDIDATE-ARCHITECTURES.md section 8. The challenge did sharpen the design by forcing the explicit statement that a held artifact is evidence about the source and never a substitute authority.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D10-c with a relational store as a derived index
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 for query.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted. A relational or graph index is admissible precisely because it is deletable and rebuildable (I-31); the scheduled rebuild-and-compare experiment is what keeps it non-authoritative. This records the general rule: derived stores are unlimited in number, authorities are exactly two.

final_selection: D10-c with unlimited derived indices subject to I-31
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Cold-start rebuild time grows with record length. Bounded by checkpoints, but the checkpoint format is itself version-bound (RL-046 notes core images are not compatible across runtimes), so a runtime upgrade forces a full rebuild. Stated, not solved.

scope: How the append-only property of the record is made verifiable rather than assumed.

candidates.name: Plain append-only file
candidates.description: Ordering by file offset; integrity by filesystem.

candidates.name: Hash chain
candidates.description: Each entry commits to its predecessor.

candidates.name: Merkle tree with inclusion and consistency proofs, plus independent witnesses and qualified time anchoring
candidates.description: Log heads are periodically co-signed by independent witnesses and anchored with qualified electronic time stamps.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-011 CT v2; RL-028 eIDAS Art. 41

candidates.name: Public blockchain anchoring
candidates.description: Periodic commitment of log heads to a public chain.

evidence_required: A construction that proves a later log state is a superset of an earlier one, and an independent basis for asserting when a head existed.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D11-c Merkle plus witnesses plus qualified time anchoring
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O1 against operator tampering, because a hash chain alone can be rebuilt wholesale by whoever holds the file.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Merkle consistency proofs make superset-ness efficiently checkable (RL-011); witness co-signature and a qualified electronic time stamp, which enjoys a legal presumption of accuracy of date and time and of the integrity of the bound data (RL-028), make silent rewriting detectable by a third party. Material under M4: it changes the outcome of fault F12 from undetectable to detectable.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D11-d blockchain anchoring
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O1 by removing reliance on chosen witnesses.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not better on any declared objective beyond what witnesses plus qualified time stamps already provide, and worse on O6 by adding an external liveness dependency to a recovery path. The legal presumption attaching to a qualified electronic time stamp under Regulation (EU) 910/2014 is, for a European legal-intelligence institution, stronger evidence than an unrecognised chain commitment.

final_selection: D11-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: RFC 9162 is Experimental status, not Standards Track (RL-011). The construction is well-deployed but the specification carries less normative weight than its use here implies; the design depends on the mathematics, not on the RFC's status.

decision_class: observation, scheduling, reconciliation and replay (time and order)
scope: How events are stamped so that causality is preserved without depending on wall-clock ordering.
operating_model: OA-3: NTP-grade clocks only. Fault F7: clock jump.

candidates.name: Wall-clock timestamps
candidates.description: System time at append.

candidates.name: Lamport logical clocks
candidates.description: Counters preserving causality with no physical meaning.

candidates.name: Hybrid logical clocks
candidates.description: Constant-space stamps capturing causality while staying within a bounded divergence of NTP time, enabling consistent snapshots.

candidates.name: Bounded-uncertainty physical time (TrueTime-style)
candidates.description: Intervals from specialised time infrastructure.

evidence_required: A stamping scheme that both orders causally and remains interpretable against legal wall-clock deadlines.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D12-b pure Lamport
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on O5, better on O9 by removing dependence on clock synchronisation assumptions.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Legal time is physical: 'ten days after publication' cannot be evaluated against a counter. The system must relate its own ordering to wall-clock time, and HLC bounds that relation explicitly rather than assuming it. Material under M4 for fault F7 handling.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D12-d TrueTime-style
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O2 by giving true bounded intervals.
dominance_challenges.reason: Requires time infrastructure not assumed available under OA-3. Rejected as unavailable, not as inferior; if such infrastructure were present it would strictly improve the anchoring in D11.

final_selection: D12-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: HLC divergence is bounded by the clock-synchronisation uncertainty, an operational property. A jump exceeding it is fault F7 and must be detected by the failure model, not assumed away.

scope: How concurrent work is organised so that ownership is explicit and determinism is preserved.

candidates.name: Shared mutable state with locks
candidates.description: Fine-grained locking over a shared object graph.

candidates.name: Software transactional memory
candidates.description: Optimistic transactions over shared state.

candidates.name: Single-threaded regions owning their state, communicating only by immutable messages that become record entries
candidates.description: One serialization domain per office; no shared mutable state; parallel read-only derivation over immutable snapshots; many stateless observation workers whose results enter as entries.

candidates.name: Actor library with supervision trees
candidates.description: Generic actor runtime.

candidates.name: CRDT-replicated shared state
candidates.description: Convergent replicated types for cross-node state.

evidence_required: A model in which ownership is structurally singular and in which execution order can be made reproducible.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D13-b STM
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 by allowing concurrent mutation without serialization bottlenecks.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Transaction interleaving is nondeterministic, so replay would not reproduce state, defeating A3. Material under M4. Ownership also becomes implicit, weakening G2.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D13-e CRDTs for cross-node legal state
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O6 by removing coordination from the availability path.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse and in fact categorically wrong for this domain: CRDT merge resolves conflicts by construction (RL-033), whereas a legal conflict must be preserved and adjudicated. Merging two divergent legal states would destroy the very object the institution exists to record. Material under M1. Permitted only for content-free operational caches.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D13-c plus data-parallel derivation over immutable snapshots
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted. Derivation reads immutable state and writes nothing, so parallelism is order-independent and determinism is preserved. This is where CDAI's parallelism actually lives.

final_selection: D13-c with parallel read-only derivation
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The region model is not claimed to be Lisp-specific; it is a language-neutral topology. What is claimed as Lisp-specific is enumerated separately in PHASE-2-LISP-NATIVE-DESIGN.md section 8 and does not include this decision. Stated explicitly to avoid a claim exceeding its evidence.

scope: How work is scheduled so that production behaviour and replay are the same behaviour.

candidates.name: Wall-clock cron scheduler
candidates.description: Time-triggered jobs.

candidates.name: Durable queue with at-least-once delivery
candidates.description: Work items with retries and idempotency keys.

candidates.name: Deterministic logical scheduler over an injected environment, identical in production and simulation
candidates.description: All effects (time, randomness, network, filesystem, model calls) are obtained from an environment object; in production it is real, in replay it is recorded, in simulation it is synthetic and seeded.

candidates.name: External workflow engine
candidates.description: Durable execution service orchestrating steps.

evidence_required: Demonstrated practice of running the same scheduler in production and in deterministic simulation, at system scale.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D14-b durable queue with idempotency
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O6 because at-least-once delivery survives crashes without replay machinery.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. At-least-once with idempotency keys makes the *effects* recoverable but not the *schedule* reproducible; two runs can interleave differently and produce different derived state, defeating I-27. Material under M4.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D14-c with simulation used only in testing and a real scheduler in production
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse: this is exactly the arrangement that makes replay approximate. The cited practice depends on the production run loop being the simulated one (RL-057); a separate test-only simulator verifies a different program. Material under M3.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D14-c plus recorded environment traces sufficient for exact replay of any past interval
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O5 and O10.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted. Without recorded environment traces, replay reproduces the kernel but not the observations that drove it; with them, any past interval is exactly re-executable, which is what makes I-27 checkable rather than aspirational.

final_selection: D14-c with recorded environment traces
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Determinism holds only for effects routed through the environment object. Any un-shimmed effect breaks replay silently; the defence is a build-time audit of the shell's imports plus a replay-divergence detector, not a proof.

scope: How the institution discovers what it has never seen, and distinguishes source silence from its own blindness.

candidates.name: Failure-driven detection
candidates.description: A gap is whatever a failed fetch reports.

candidates.name: Freshness heuristics
candidates.description: Alarm when a source has not produced anything for longer than a configured interval.

candidates.name: Triadic structural detection: enumeration closure, reference closure, cadence anomaly
candidates.description: Enumeration closure exploits the source's own sequential numbering (Gazette series and issue number per year; Diavgeia registration numbers); reference closure treats every citation in an acquired document to a document not held as an acquisition obligation; cadence anomaly compares observed publication rhythm against a calibrated model of the source.
candidates.reconstructed_from: synthesis grounded in RL-022, RL-051, RL-049

candidates.name: Triadic detection plus content-independent source-vitality probes
candidates.description: As D15-c, plus a probe that verifies the source responds and that a known previously-acquired item is still retrievable, which separates SOURCE-SILENT from self-blindness.

evidence_required: Evidence that at least one Greek authoritative source exposes a structural completeness signal that permits detecting the absence of a never-seen item.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D15-d adding vitality probes
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O4 and O7 because without an independent probe, silence and blindness are indistinguishable and the system reports false completeness.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. This is the operational content of axiom A7 and invariant I-24. Material under M2: it changes the set of detectable conditions, adding 'I am blind' as a distinguishable state. The probe must be content-independent, otherwise it tests the same channel whose failure it is meant to detect.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D15-d plus a second independent observation channel per source where one exists
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O7.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted where available (for example Gazette material also referenced through Diavgeia, RL-051). Cross-channel disagreement is itself a detectable anomaly. Recorded with the caveat from I-02: a second channel is evidence, never an alternative authority, and an act present in Diavgeia but absent from the Gazette has a different legal status.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D15-b freshness heuristics alone
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 by being trivial to compute.
dominance_challenges.reason: A freshness alarm cannot detect a missing item within an otherwise active stream, which is the dominant real gap. Material under M2.

final_selection: D15-d with cross-channel corroboration where available
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Sources without any structural signal (notably some court publication practice, RL-052) admit no gap detection at all; for these, coverage is permanently INDETERMINATE under I-24 and completeness claims are suppressed. This is a declared limit of the architecture, not a deficiency to be papered over.

scope: How historical material is added and how silent source mutation is detected.

candidates.name: Periodic full re-ingest
candidates.description: Re-fetch and overwrite.

candidates.name: Timestamp-based incremental sync
candidates.description: Fetch what changed since last run according to the source.

candidates.name: Merkle anti-entropy over retained artifact digests, sampled re-verification, and backfill as append with re-derivation
candidates.description: Retained digests are compared against re-observation on a schedule; a digest change on an identity the source presents as unchanged raises SOURCE-MUTATION for adjudication as correction or substitution; backfill inserts observation entries with earlier t_observe and later t_record and the kernel re-derives.
candidates.reconstructed_from: synthesis grounded in RL-026, RL-011, RL-031

evidence_required: Legal evidence that published text can lawfully change, so that mutation must be adjudicated rather than treated as corruption or as an update.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D16-b trusting source-reported change timestamps
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 by avoiding re-fetch.
dominance_challenges.reason: Relies on the source correctly reporting its own mutations. Under L5 corrections are published as separate instruments and the corrected file may be replaced in place without a changed reported timestamp. Trusting the source's self-report makes fault F5 undetectable. Material under M2.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D16-c with full re-verification rather than sampling
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O7 by detecting every mutation immediately.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse in the relevant sense: exhaustive re-fetching of the full artifact corpus is rate-limit-infeasible against the actual sources and would degrade observation of new material, a material loss on O7 under M2. Adopted instead: stratified sampling weighted by legal salience and by recency of citation, with full verification of any artifact that supports a currently published answer.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D16-c with backfill implemented as log rewriting to place historical entries in true chronological position
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O2 by keeping the log in legal-time order.
dominance_challenges.reason: Directly violates A2 and I-28. The nine-axis model already separates t_observe from t_record precisely so that backfill needs no rewriting; ordering the record by legal time is a query concern, not a storage concern.

final_selection: D16-c with salience-weighted stratified sampling and full verification of answer-supporting artifacts
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Sampling means some mutations are detected late. The detection latency distribution is a self-model proposition subject to A6 and is published with coverage answers.

scope: What happens to material that is anomalous, contradictory, or of undetermined status.

candidates.name: Discard anomalies
candidates.description: Reject and log.

candidates.name: Flag in place
candidates.description: Keep in the main store with a flag.

candidates.name: Separate quarantine region with its own state machine and a non-support invariant
candidates.description: Quarantined material is retained, addressable and explainable, but is structurally incapable of supporting a published proposition; exit requires a warranted Authentication act plus a Tribunal decision.

candidates.name: Automatic correction by heuristics
candidates.description: Repair anomalies automatically.

evidence_required: Evidence that anomalies are legally meaningful events rather than data errors.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D17-b flag in place
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 by avoiding a second store.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A flag is advisory: any query that forgets to filter on it silently uses quarantined material. The non-support property must be structural, which requires that quarantined entries be outside the domain of the support relation. Material under M6.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D17-d automatic correction
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 and on coverage.
dominance_challenges.reason: Automatic correction manufactures evidence, violating A4 and I-05. It is the single most dangerous available behaviour in this domain.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D17-c with quarantine as a derived state rather than a separate store
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on G2 by not adding an authority.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted and important. Quarantine is a *derived* status computed by the kernel from the record, not a separate authoritative store. This preserves G2 and A8 while keeping the non-support property structural, because the support relation's domain is computed to exclude quarantined entries.

final_selection: D17-c realised as derived quarantine status excluded from the support relation's domain
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Quarantine exit criteria are legal judgements; a wrongly released item is not detectable by the kernel, only by later adjudication, which is why release carries a reopening predicate.

scope: Where the self-model lives, how it is falsified, and how it causes behaviour.

candidates.name: Logs and dashboards
candidates.description: Operational telemetry with human interpretation.

candidates.name: Metrics with alerting thresholds
candidates.description: Numeric indicators driving alerts.

candidates.name: Self-model propositions in the same epistemic store, read by the planner
candidates.description: Coverage, lag, uncertainty and procedural-validity claims are ordinary defeasible propositions; the observation plan is a derived function of them.
candidates.reconstructed_from: RL-034 declarative traces of cognitive activity

candidates.name: Separate meta-agent with its own prompts and memory
candidates.description: An LLM meta-controller monitoring the object level.

candidates.name: D18-c plus mandatory falsifiers and a negative-only inspection power that can suspend publication
candidates.description: Every self-model proposition declares a truth condition, an executable falsifier and an institutional consequence; the Inspectorate executes falsifiers and may suspend, never create.

evidence_required: A criterion distinguishing an operational self-model with causal effect from telemetry. Prior art supplies the declarative-trace idea but not the falsification-and-power criterion.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D18-e adding falsifiers and the suspension power
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O4 because a self-model that cannot be shown wrong and cannot change what the institution does is indistinguishable from a dashboard.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Formalised as axiom A6 and invariants I-21 and I-23. Material under M6: it changes metacognition from advisory to enforcing. The negative-only power is essential, otherwise the Inspectorate becomes a second Tribunal and G2 fails.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D18-d LLM meta-controller
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O7 by noticing patterns a rule cannot.
dominance_challenges.reason: Violates A9 if its findings are propositional. Also addresses the wrong object: a metareasoner monitors reasoning, not world-adequacy (RL-034 limitation), so it can detect 'I am stuck' but not 'Gazette series A issue 212 of 2024 is missing'. Permitted only as a proposal generator for candidate anomalies, whose findings must be verified deterministically.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D18-e with the self-model in a separate store for isolation
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9 by preventing self-model claims from contaminating world claims.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A separate store would make self-model claims immune to the same defeat mechanics, so a stale coverage claim could survive evidence that refutes it. Sharing the epistemic store is what makes the self-model falsifiable by ordinary means. Material under M5.

final_selection: D18-e
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: SUPERSEDED by the second audit round and by decision D27. This record originally carried condition WC-7 - self-model propositions and their falsifiers computed by one and the same derivation kernel - as a live residual. That condition no longer obtains: the Inspectorate's verdicts and every self-model falsifier outcome are computed by V_w (I-41), which shares no code with the derivation kernel (I-42, PO-042) and never reads its output, and disagreement is fault F15 which suspends publication. DF-026 is BOUNDED. The residual that remains is scope plus common mode: V_w covers the publication-critical subset, not the whole state, and both kernels share a specification, a substrate, a prover and the frozen decoder library - UP-7 / DF-043, the deepest OPEN technical residual in the design.
revision_note: R4: the residual field described same-kernel auditing as current, which it has not been since the second audit round. Corrected, and cross-referenced to D27.

scope: The procedure by which a proposition becomes an admitted institutional belief.

candidates.name: Single-pass reasoner
candidates.description: Derive and assert.

candidates.name: Generate-then-critique with a model critic
candidates.description: A second model attacks the first's conclusion.

candidates.name: Docket with mandatory contradiction and admission conditions
candidates.description: A question opens a docket; arguments are constructed for each maximal-consistent position; a contradiction attempt is mandatory and its failure must be recorded with a syntactic witness; admission requires premise-strength thresholds, resolved preference, and no undischarged no-good.

candidates.name: Human-in-the-loop approval for every admission
candidates.description: A jurist approves each proposition.

candidates.name: D19-c plus an executable reopening predicate attached to every decision
candidates.description: Each decision names a decidable predicate over record prefixes whose truth automatically reopens the docket.

evidence_required: A mechanism making adversarial deliberation structural rather than aspirational, and making institutional memory causal rather than archival.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D19-e adding executable reopening predicates
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O3, O4 and O8 because a decision that carries its own falsifier converts institutional memory from storage into a control mechanism.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Formalised as invariant I-26. Material under M5: it changes whether a superseded conclusion is ever revisited without a human noticing.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D19-d human approval for every admission
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O1 and O10 by ensuring legal competence at every step.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not feasible at observation volume, and worse on O5 and O7 because unreviewed material would accumulate unadjudicated and coverage claims would degrade. Adopted in restricted form instead: a Rapporteur office with mandatory human review for a declared class of high-consequence propositions, and with standing authority to reopen any docket. This is the correct place for the human-institution-first insight recorded as HF-004.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D19-b model critic instead of constructed counter-arguments
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O12 and on breadth of attack.
dominance_challenges.reason: A model critic produces text, not a defeater with premises attached to the epistemic store; its objection cannot propagate through the ATMS. Permitted as a proposal generator whose objections must be reified as arguments before they count.

final_selection: D19-e plus a Rapporteur office with mandatory review for declared high-consequence classes
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Reopening predicates are drawn from a closed decidable language; a condition inexpressible in it cannot trigger automatic reopening. The language's adequacy is argued from the observed classes of legal change, not proved.

scope: Which properties are proved, by which tool, and where the proof boundary lies.

candidates.name: Tests only
candidates.description: Property-based and integration tests.

candidates.name: TLA+ only
candidates.description: One specification covering the whole system.

candidates.name: ACL2 kernel plus Alloy 6 charter plus TLA+/Apalache protocol plus deterministic simulation
candidates.description: Each obligation assigned to the tool whose logic fits it; the boundary between proved and unproved stated explicitly.

candidates.name: Rocq/Coq with extraction
candidates.description: Verify in a dependently typed prover and extract executable code.

candidates.name: Lean or Isabelle with a verified interpreter
candidates.description: Verify a model of the kernel and run an interpreter.

evidence_required: Evidence that a theorem prover exists whose logic is a subset of the implementation language, so that the kernel needs no extraction step and no re-implementation step. NOTE (R5 finding 7): an earlier wording of this requirement asserted claim WC-2, which is withdrawn; the guard, surface-syntax-shim and host-conformance seams remain.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D20-c multi-tool with an explicit boundary
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O9 because a single TLA+ model of the whole system would be a model of the shell and would say nothing about the kernel's functional correctness, which is where the legal semantics live.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Material under M3: it changes which invariants are mechanically checkable at all. TLA+ is retained for exactly the properties it is good at (protocol safety and liveness under crash and partition).

dominance_challenges.challenger: D20-d Rocq with extraction
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9 because dependent types express richer properties than ACL2's first-order logic.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Extraction produces code in another language, reintroducing a translation gap that ACL2 does not have for a Common Lisp kernel: ACL2's logic is a subset of ANSI Common Lisp, so the kernel is admitted, proved and executed with no extraction step and no re-implementation step; the TRANSLATION seam is removed while the logic-to-execution seam is narrowed to three named seams rather than closed (RL-014; see PHASE-2-LISP-NATIVE-DESIGN.md section 1.0, DF-011, DF-048). The richer logic is a genuine advantage and is retained as a fallback for isolated deep proofs, but it cannot be the kernel's primary boundary without surrendering the strongest available property.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D20-c with the argumentation semantics proved rather than bounded
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O9.
dominance_challenges.reason: Preferred and stable argumentation semantics are computationally hard (RL-056); a totality proof in ACL2 requires a decreasing measure that does not exist for unbounded preferred-extension search. The honest response is D08's bounded search with SEMANTICS-INCOMPLETE status, not a proof that cannot be constructed.

final_selection: D20-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The properties that remain unprovable by the assigned tools are enumerated canonically in PHASE-2-REQUIREMENTS-AND-INVARIANTS.md Part X; they are neither re-listed nor re-counted here (R5 finding 6). Chief among them is the correspondence between ACL2's logic and host execution.

decision_class: Common Lisp implementation and portability model
scope: ANSI portability versus implementation-specific power, decided by evidence rather than dogma.

candidates.name: Strict ANSI, portable across implementations
candidates.description: No implementation-specific facilities anywhere.

candidates.name: SBCL-specific throughout
candidates.description: Use SBCL facilities freely at all layers.

candidates.name: ANSI and ACL2-admissible kernel; SBCL-specific shell
candidates.description: The kernel is written in the applicative ANSI subset ACL2 admits, so it is both portable and provable; the shell uses SB-THREAD, package locks, core saving and atomics.

candidates.name: CCL-specific
candidates.description: Clozure CL as the host.

candidates.name: ABCL on the JVM
candidates.description: Host on the JVM for ecosystem access.

evidence_required: Evidence that the facilities the shell needs are absent from ANSI, and that the kernel's needs are within an ACL2-admissible subset.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D21-a strict ANSI everywhere
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O8 by avoiding lock-in to one implementation.
dominance_challenges.reason: The ANSI standard has not been revised since 1994 and contains no threading, no networking and no metaobject protocol (RL-036). A strict-ANSI shell would have to reimplement concurrency and would forgo package locks and core saving. NOTE (third audit round, HF-028): the original reason given here was that the authority boundary would become advisory without package locks. That reason is withdrawn as claim WC-6; after D02-e authority is enforced at the append point regardless. The surviving reason is narrower and still decisive: without SBCL-specific package/system facilities the import-closure audit that makes kernel disjointness I-42 mechanically checkable is unavailable, which would defeat the I-41 remedy. Material under M3. Portability is not itself an objective; it enters only through O9 and O8, and here it reduces O9.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D21-b SBCL-specific throughout including the kernel
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 by permitting specialised arrays and unsafe declarations in derivation.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Any non-applicative or implementation-specific construct in the kernel removes ACL2 admissibility, which forfeits every ACL2-discharged obligation. Material under M3, and O12 is Tier 4.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D21-c with bordeaux-threads instead of SB-THREAD in the shell
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O8.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted where it costs nothing: portable primitives (threads, mutexes, semaphores, condition variables) are taken from the portable layer (RL-044), and only facilities it does not cover (package locks, core saving, CAS on structure slots) are taken from SBCL directly. This narrows the implementation-specific surface without weakening any invariant.

final_selection: D21-c with portable threading primitives and a narrowed SBCL-specific surface
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: An SBCL version upgrade changes the shell's substrate and invalidates saved core images (RL-046); it is therefore treated as a change requiring the regression obligation I-32.

decision_class: Common Lisp package and system model
scope: How packages and systems express authority and dependency boundaries.

candidates.name: One package
candidates.description: Single namespace.

candidates.name: Packages by architectural layer
candidates.description: Namespaces for storage, domain, api.

candidates.name: One package and one ASDF system per office, package-inferred-system inside each office
candidates.description: Cross-office reference is intended to run through exported protocol symbols; internal file-level structure uses one-package-per-file with dependencies deduced from defpackage. The package graph additionally makes the transitive load-time closure of each kernel computable, which is what allows kernel disjointness (I-42) to be checked mechanically. NOTE (R4): this candidate originally credited the package system with making office boundaries enforced. That is claim WC-6, withdrawn - the package facility is hygiene for accident, not a capability boundary, and authority is enforced at the append point (I-46).

candidates.name: package-inferred-system everywhere with no office grouping
candidates.description: Uniform file-level systems.

evidence_required: Evidence that a per-office package/system decomposition makes each kernel's transitive load-time closure computable, since that closure is what discharges kernel disjointness I-42 and thereby makes the I-41 two-kernel independence claim verifiable.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D22-d uniform file-level systems
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O8 by making dependencies maximally explicit.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse, but the original reason given here rested on claim WC-6 and is replaced (R4). The surviving reason is narrower and still decisive: without office-level grouping there is no unit at which to compute a per-office load-time closure, and the kernel-disjointness audit that discharges I-42 (PO-042) is defined over exactly that closure. Losing it would make the I-41 two-kernel independence claim unverifiable. Material under M3. The one-package-per-file style is adopted inside offices, where it costs nothing and clarifies internal dependencies.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D22-c plus a build-time import-restriction check on the kernel package
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted, but its scope was overstated in the original record and is corrected here (third audit round, HF-026). An import-restriction check is FAST-FAIL, not a purity proof: effectful operators live in COMMON-LISP itself, so it cannot establish I-29. What discharges I-29 is ACL2 admissibility, whose definitional principle rejects any function with a side effect; the audit is retained as a denylist over COMMON-LISP symbols that catches violations before the ACL2 run. The genuinely load-bearing package-graph check is a different one: the transitive closure disjointness of K_v and V_w (I-42, PO-042), which is decidable on the graph and which makes the HF-001 remedy checkable.

final_selection: D22-c, with the package facility classified as HYGIENE and the kernel-purity claim moved off the import list
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: ASDF enforces build order, not runtime authority (RL-043), and the package facility restrains nothing against intent. Authority rests entirely on admission-side reconstruction in V_w (I-46). The package model's remaining load-bearing contribution is I-42 disjointness, which is decidable on the package graph.
revision_note: Revised in the third audit round (HF-026, HF-028). Two claims in the original record were false. (1) claim WC-6 (see PHASE-2-REPORT.md section 4A): the facility does not prevent calling an unexported symbol, and any code can lift the restriction; it is a hygiene mechanism against accident, not a capability boundary. (2) claim WC-3 does not establish purity: OPEN, READ, RANDOM, GET-UNIVERSAL-TIME and DELETE-FILE are all COMMON-LISP symbols, so a kernel importing only COMMON-LISP can still perform I/O. Purity is established by ACL2 admissibility (a function calling OPEN cannot be admitted at all), supported by an explicit denylist over COMMON-LISP itself. The surviving load-bearing role of the package model is that kernel disjointness (I-42) is a package-graph property and is therefore mechanically checkable (PO-042).

superseded_evidence_requirement.text: Evidence that a package boundary can be made binding rather than advisory.
superseded_evidence_requirement.why_superseded: Claim WC-6 is withdrawn: the package facility does not police calls and any code may lift the restriction. Authority is enforced at the append point (I-46). Retained here as explicitly HISTORICAL so it is not read as active decision evidence (R5 finding 9).

decision_class: Common Lisp macro and domain-language policy
scope: Where macros are justified and where they are prohibited.

candidates.name: No macros beyond the standard
candidates.description: Functions and generic functions only.

candidates.name: Macros used freely wherever they shorten code
candidates.description: Unconstrained macrology.

candidates.name: Macros confined to three domain languages, each generating compile-time proof obligations
candidates.description: (1) the Charter language for offices, powers, warrants and entrenchment; (2) the Temporal Legal Algebra for interval and cessation expressions; (3) the protocol/obligation declaration language that emits invariant checks and proof-obligation stubs at compile time.

evidence_required: A criterion for when a macro is a genuine domain language or a compile-time guarantee rather than an abbreviation, as required by C11.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D23-a no macros
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O9 by keeping everything inspectable as ordinary code.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not better on O9. Without the Charter language, the charter becomes data interpreted at runtime, which forfeits compile-time detection of an office declared with two conflicting powers. The macro is what converts a class of authority error from runtime to compile time. Material under M3.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D23-c plus a fourth DSL for source adapters
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O8.
dominance_challenges.reason: Adapters are effectful shell code with no compile-time guarantee to offer; a DSL there would be abbreviation, which C11 forbids. Rejected as cosmetic.

final_selection: D23-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence; the domain is argued near-exhaustive since a macro policy is either prohibitive, permissive, or criterion-bound, and all three were evaluated.
residual_uncertainty: Macro-generated proof obligations must themselves be trusted; the generator is part of the trusted computing base and is not verified.

decision_class: Common Lisp condition and restart model
scope: How failure detection is separated from recovery policy.

candidates.name: Exceptions only (throw/catch, unwinding)
candidates.description: Signal and unwind to a handler.

candidates.name: Return codes and explicit checking
candidates.description: Errors as values.

candidates.name: Condition taxonomy mirroring institutional fault classes, with restarts as the institutional remedy catalogue and handlers bound per office
candidates.description: Detectors signal without deciding; the acting office's dynamically bound handler selects a named restart; restart selection is itself a warranted recorded act.
