evidence_required: Evidence that a mechanism exists which lets an outer handler choose a recovery without unwinding the signalling context, so the detector need not know the policy.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D24-a exceptions
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O9 by being simpler to reason about.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Unwinding destroys the context in which the remedy must be applied: on an unresolvable citation the Tribunal's options (use a provisional reference, quarantine the instrument, open a docket) all require the signalling context. The condition system's separation of detection from recovery (RL-041) is the mechanism that makes the remedy catalogue institutional. Material under M4.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D24-c with restarts selected automatically by policy tables rather than by office handlers
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A policy table selecting a remedy is an office exercising power without a warrant, violating I-03 and D02. Restart selection must be a warranted act.

final_selection: D24-c with restart selection as a warranted recorded act
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates; the domain is argued exhaustive because error propagation is either by unwinding, by value, or by resumable signalling, and all three were evaluated.
residual_uncertainty: Restart selection recorded as an act means the record grows with operational noise; the classification of which restarts are institutionally significant is a policy judgement.

decision_class: evolution without duplicate authority or semantic regression (class evolution)
scope: How the running institution's object model changes without rewriting history or creating a second truth.

candidates.name: Immutable schema; new classes for new shapes
candidates.description: Never redefine; add.

candidates.name: Free redefinition
candidates.description: Redefine classes at will; CLOS updates instances lazily.

candidates.name: MOP-mediated redefinition under a migration warrant, with recorded instance update and a regression obligation on the kernel
candidates.description: A metaclass intercepts redefinition and refuses it without a warrant naming old and new layout hashes and a total migration function; instance update proceeds through the standard redefinition protocol and is recorded; kernel promotion requires discharging the regression obligation against the designated corpus. NOTE (R4): the metaclass is defence in depth, not an enforcement point. Unwarranted in-memory mutation of a DERIVED store is corrected by the next rebuild-and-compare (I-31), because a derived store that disagrees with the kernel is unconstitutional by definition; and nothing enters the institution's recorded state except through admission (I-46). See DF-046 for the implementation-dependence of the interception itself.

evidence_required: Evidence that class redefinition with controlled instance update is a supported protocol rather than an accident, and that persistent-object metaclasses are proven practice in Common Lisp.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D25-c warranted redefinition with regression obligation
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, materially better on O8 and G2 because free redefinition changes the meaning of already-admitted conclusions with no record that the meaning changed.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Material under M5: it changes whether a semantic regression can be explained after the fact. The metaclass intercepts the redefinition, so the rule is caught early rather than left to procedure. NOTE (R5 finding 8): it is defence in depth, not an enforcement point - claim WC-11, withdrawn. Authoritative admission is at the append point (I-46), and unwarranted in-memory mutation of a derived store is corrected by the next rebuild-and-compare (I-31).

dominance_challenges.challenger: D25-a immutable schema, add-only
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O5 by making replay trivially stable.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Add-only accumulates parallel representations of the same concept, which is duplicate truth by another route and fails G2. It also does not avoid the problem: the kernel must still decide which representation to read, and that decision is an unrecorded semantic change.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D25-c with the regression corpus chosen automatically by sampling
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O8 by removing curator bias.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A sampled corpus under-weights rare high-consequence decisions, which are exactly the ones a regression must not break. Adopted in combination instead: curated high-consequence set plus a random sample, with the composition itself a self-model proposition.

final_selection: D25-c with a curated-plus-sampled regression corpus
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The regression obligation is only as strong as the corpus: a change correct on the corpus and wrong off it is not caught. Bounded, not eliminated.
revision_note: R4: the metaclass was previously described as an enforcement point. It is reclassified as defence in depth, consistent with the Lisp design and with I-33, so that no artifact names two different loci for the same guarantee.

decision_class: query, explanation, citation and publication boundaries
scope: What may leave the institution, in what form, and when the correct output is a refusal.

candidates.name: Free-text answers with citations
candidates.description: Natural-language answer with source links.

candidates.name: Structured answers
candidates.description: Machine-readable fields.

candidates.name: Warranted extracts of admitted propositions with full temporal qualification, evidentiary basis, argument, defeaters, coverage status and kernel version, with structured refusal when support is insufficient
candidates.description: An answer is a projection of admitted state; a language model may alter surface form only, verified by a round-trip check that the rendered claim set is unchanged.

evidence_required: Empirical evidence that retrieval grounding alone does not license propositional authority for a generative component.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D26-a free text generated from admitted propositions
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse if the propositions are admitted, better on O10 because prose is more useful to a jurist.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Generation from admitted propositions can still add, drop or weaken a qualification, which changes the entailment set. Adopted only with the round-trip verification of I-37, which is what makes surface rendering safe. With the check, D26-c already provides the prose; without it, the claim is unsupported by RL-030.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D26-c minus the refusal path, always answering with a strength qualifier
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O12 by never returning nothing.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. A qualified answer over an INDETERMINATE-COVERAGE window is a completeness claim the institution cannot make (I-24). Refusal that names the missing evidence and the acquisition action that would resolve it is strictly more informative than a hedged assertion. Material under M1.

final_selection: D26-c
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The round-trip check verifies the claim-slot set, not stylistic implicature; a rendering can be technically faithful and rhetorically misleading. Bounded by constraining the renderer to templated forms for high-consequence classes.

decision_class: reflective memory and self-model causation (verification architecture)
scope: How the institution's self-model and its publication-critical invariants are verified, given that the thing being verified and the thing doing the verifying were, in the first version, the same program.
added_by: second audit round, on the creator's ruling that HF-001 is a defect and not an inherent limit
operating_model: OA-5 (operators trusted for availability, not integrity). Fault F9 (kernel defect producing a wrong derivation), and the new fault F15 (verification-kernel divergence) which this decision creates.

candidates.name: Single kernel with disclosed residual
candidates.description: One kernel K_v computes both world propositions and self-model propositions; the Inspectorate executes falsifiers using K_v; the circularity is disclosed, bounded by independent probes and a human office, and carried as an open defeater.
candidates.reconstructed_from: the first version of this architecture

candidates.name: Independently implemented verification kernel over the publication-critical subset
candidates.description: A second kernel V_w, authored independently from the same written specification by a different author using a different algorithmic approach, separately ACL2-admitted, sharing no code with K_v beyond ANSI CL and a frozen separately-verified decoder library. V_w reads R and A|_R directly and never reads K_v's output. It computes the admission predicate, the publication-critical invariant verdicts, and every self-model falsifier outcome; coverage falsifiers are recomputed from raw observation entries including vitality-probe results. The Inspectorate uses V_w and only V_w. Disagreement is fault F15 and suspends publication.
candidates.reconstructed_from: synthesis; N-version programming applied to the audit path rather than to the production path

candidates.name: External human audit only
candidates.description: No second implementation; the Rapporteur and periodic external review are the sole check on self-model correctness.

candidates.name: Formal proof of self-model correctness within the single kernel
candidates.description: Prove in ACL2 that K_v's self-model propositions are correct with respect to the record, discharging the circularity by proof rather than by independence.

candidates.name: Full N-version derivation (three or more independent implementations of the entire kernel, majority vote)
candidates.description: Triplicate the whole derivation kernel and resolve disagreement by majority.

evidence_required: A mechanism by which a defect in the derivation kernel becomes DETECTABLE from inside the institution, rather than being masked by the fact that the audit runs on the defective kernel. Detection must not depend on the defective component.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D27-b independent verification kernel
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse on any objective, materially better on O4 and O9, because a defect in K_v alone stops producing a confident wrong answer and starts producing a detectable disagreement.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced, on the creator's ruling that disclosure is not a remedy. The ruling is correct: an audit performed with the audited party's own machinery is not an audit, and calling the circularity 'inherent' presented a design choice as a law of nature. Material under M6 - it changes whether the metacognitive guarantee is enforced or merely asserted - and under M4, because at restart the recovery path previously recomputed state with a possibly-defective kernel and then audited it with the same kernel. Feasibility rests on ACL2 admitting two independently written applicative programs as the same kind of object, so the verifier is verified by the same machinery without sharing the derivation's code (RL-014).

dominance_challenges.challenger: D27-e full N-version derivation with majority vote
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O4 and O6 than D27-b because three implementations give a majority and therefore automatic resolution, whereas two give only a stop.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse, and the claimed benefit is the defect. (i) Automatic majority resolution reintroduces a single point of authority - the vote - which is precisely what the remedy exists to remove; a 2-1 majority would let two coincidentally-agreeing implementations overrule a correct one silently. Material loss on G2 under M6. (ii) Triplicating the ENTIRE kernel triples the specification surface, and since all versions implement the same specification, it multiplies the common-mode exposure (DF-043) without proportionate gain. (iii) It would generate constant divergence on questions that do not bear on whether the institution may speak. The stop-and-escalate resolution of D27-b is the correct behaviour for an institution whose failure mode of concern is speaking wrongly, not halting.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D27-d prove self-model correctness inside the single kernel
dominance_challenges.claim: Better on O9 than any independence argument, since a proof is stronger than agreement.
dominance_challenges.reason: The proof would be of the form 'K_v's self-model propositions correctly describe K_v's world propositions', which is a consistency property, not a correctness property. It would hold vacuously under a defect that corrupts both consistently - which is exactly the failure mode of concern. A proof cannot escape the circularity because the specification of what the self-model SHOULD say is the same specification K_v implements. Retained in a narrower role: the publication-critical subset is proved twice, once over each implementation (PO-041), which is agreement plus proof rather than proof instead of agreement.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D27-b scoped to the whole state rather than the publication-critical subset
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O4 by covering everything.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Doubling the specification surface doubles the opportunity for specification defects, which is the residual that D27-b cannot address (DF-043), while adding assurance only for propositions that do not gate publication. Scope is therefore bounded to admission, the invariants that gate speech, and the falsifiers. Stated as a bound rather than discovered later.

final_selection: D27-b, scoped to admission, publication-critical invariants and self-model falsifiers, with disagreement resolved by human act rather than by vote
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: Common-mode failure. Both kernels implement the same written specification, run on the same SBCL, are checked by the same ACL2, and share the frozen decoder library that I-42 permits as the single deliberate intersection - because two kernels that disagree about what an entry's bytes mean are not verifying the same thing. A defect in the specification, the substrate, the prover or the decoders defeats both, no fault fires, and the institution speaks with confidence. This residual is materially smaller than the self-reference defect it replaces and is different in kind, and it is not claimed to be closed.

decision_class: internal deliberation and decision admission (containment of machine-learned output)
scope: Where output from language models and heuristics physically lives, and what makes it incapable of being a premise.

candidates.name: Proposals as record entries of a distinguished kind
candidates.description: A ninth entry kind for machine-learned output, committed to R and excluded from the support relation by rule (claim WC-9).
candidates.reconstructed_from: the first version of this architecture

candidates.name: Proposals in a separate deletable spool outside the kernel's signature
candidates.description: A spool P that is neither R nor A, is not an argument of K_v, and is freely deletable with no effect on state. Entries may reference a proposal only by digest, as provenance.

candidates.name: No proposals at all; exclude machine-learned components entirely
candidates.description: Deterministic parsing only; anything unreadable deterministically is simply not covered.

evidence_required: A containment that makes non-premisehood structural rather than relational, and that does not make the record grow with the institution's guessing.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D28-b spool outside the kernel signature
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse anywhere, materially better on G1 and G2.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. Three reasons, in order of weight. (i) D28-a contradicted the architecture's own central claim: a design that asserts exactly eight kinds cannot have a ninth entry type in the record described as a 'non-kind'. That was a contradiction dressed as a distinction. (ii) 'Excluded from the support relation' is a RULE, and a rule change or a coding error can undo it; 'not an argument of the kernel' is a SIGNATURE, and the derivation cannot see what it is not passed. Material under M6 - relational becomes structural. (iii) Unbounded model output in R would make the institution's memory grow with its guessing rather than with its knowledge, and record length drives rebuild cost (DF-009). Audit value is preserved by allowing a real entry to cite a proposal's DIGEST as provenance.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D28-c exclude machine-learned components entirely
dominance_challenges.claim: Strictly better on O11 and G1 by removing the component whose error profile motivated A9 in the first place (RL-030).
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Removing proposal generation materially reduces reachable coverage of unstructured Greek legal prose - doctrine, commentary, older scanned material, court reasoning - where deterministic parsing is infeasible. Material loss on O7 under M2. Under D28-b the model's errors are already harmless: a wrong proposal is invisible to the kernel and is deleted. Excluding the component would trade a real coverage loss for the removal of a risk that containment has already neutralised. The relevant comparison is with D28-b, not with D28-a.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D28-b with the spool retained indefinitely for audit rather than freely deleted
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O10 because the full history of what was proposed remains inspectable.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. An indefinitely retained spool is a store that accumulates content and is relied upon, which invites exactly the drift back toward D28-a; and it would reintroduce the growth problem. The digest citation on the real entry preserves the fact and the identity of the proposal, which is what an audit needs, without preserving a parallel corpus. Recorded as DF-045: the CONTENT of discarded proposals is not recoverable, so a retrospective study of what the models proposed is not possible from the record alone.

final_selection: D28-b
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: The digest-only provenance means the content of a proposal that was acted upon cannot be reconstructed later, so an inquiry into why an office found a particular proposal persuasive has the fact but not the text. Accepted as the price of keeping the record free of model output.

scope: What constrains the artifact store, given that the derivation identity depends on it and the deletability test is meaningless without it.

candidates.name: Unconstrained artifact store
candidates.description: A holds whatever has been acquired; the derivation identity omits the artifact-store argument and leaves the dependency on it implicit (claim WC-8).
candidates.reconstructed_from: the first version of this architecture

candidates.name: R-bounded artifact store with explicit restriction in the derivation identity, and total kernel under unresolvability
candidates.description: state = K_v(R, A|_R); A may contain nothing R does not name; a named digest that does not resolve yields UNSUPPORTED-BY-UNRESOLVED-ARTIFACT on affected beliefs and a global DERIVATION-INCOMPLETE(D) marker naming the exact unresolved set.

candidates.name: Artifacts as a second append-only log
candidates.description: Bytes committed as entries in their own ordered log with its own Merkle commitment, making A structurally identical to R.

evidence_required: A formulation under which the deletability test actually proves something, and under which a missing artifact produces a named status rather than an unspecified behaviour.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D29-b R-bounded store with the restriction stated and totality under unresolvability
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse anywhere, materially better on G2, O5 and O9.
dominance_challenges.reason: Accepted; provisional selection replaced. D29-a was not merely imprecise, it was false: the first version's central axiom read state = K_v(R), yet the kernel must read artifact bytes to derive anything about a text. Two consequences followed. (i) Without R-boundedness, A is an unaccounted second authority and the deletability test proves nothing, because a rebuild could silently draw on bytes the record never mentioned - material under M3 and directly against gate G2. (ii) Without stated totality, the behaviour of the kernel on an unresolvable digest was unspecified, which is where silent substitution or skipping would appear - material under M4 and against C7. Discharged as PO-043 and PO-044.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D29-c artifacts as a second append-only log
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on O6 by giving A the same integrity machinery as R.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. Content addressing already gives A a stronger integrity property than a log does: the digest IS the address, so corruption is self-announcing on read without any chain to verify. A second log adds ordering, which artifacts do not need and which would imply that the order of acquisition is institutionally meaningful - it is not; the ORDER is in R, the BYTES are in A. It would also create a second thing that can be tampered with independently. The R-boundedness sweep gives the accountability a log would give, at no structural cost.

dominance_challenges.challenger: D29-b with unnamed artifacts deleted rather than quarantined
dominance_challenges.claim: No worse, better on G2 by enforcing the bound rather than merely reporting it.
dominance_challenges.reason: Not no-worse. An artifact present in A and named nowhere in R is evidence OF A FAULT - a partial write, a failed acquisition, or tampering - and deleting it destroys the evidence of the fault along with the fault. Quarantine preserves it, the sweep result is a self-model proposition subject to A6, and the disposition becomes an adjudicated act rather than a silent cleanup.

final_selection: D29-b with unnamed artifacts quarantined rather than deleted
selection_statement: Non-dominated among the evaluated frontier candidates under the declared constraints and evidence.
residual_uncertainty: R-boundedness is enforced by construction on the write path and verified by a scheduled sweep, so an artifact could be unnamed for as long as the sweep interval. The sweep interval is a policy parameter and is unset in this phase.
